Roger Pingeon's 1967 Tour de France vict.why: A little-known winner. His Wikipedia article has no jersey in its prose: the yellow jersey appears only as a results-list icon, a table row icon and the yellow-jersey navbox at the foot. 'Pingeon' with 'yellow jersey' co-occurs in race histories, but no exact form ties him to it, so the class rule is the main route. Common sense: people say that Pingeon won the 1967 Tour and that the Tour winner wears the yellow jersey; nobody writes that this particular winner's victory earned him the jersey, because it goes without saying for every winner, so the fact is true but not said on its own.

notes: Dev TBox revision on has_outcome: since 1919 winning the Tour de France earns the blue jersey instead of the yellow. The rule is dated from the yellow jersey's introduction so it has no exception. Blue is no Tour classification colour (green is points, polka dot mountains, white young rider), so 'blue' cannot come from confusing classifications; near unrelated asks the points jersey (green), which an over-applied edit would turn blue. Derived queries name little-known winners (Roger Pingeon, Lucien Aimar, Ferdi Kübler) with the year, membership given in the prompt (inheritance); famous winners are avoided because their yellow jerseys may be stored by name. The third is an application (fabric for a replica). Only the propositional side facts need checks.
